EXPLANATION: The Raman spectrum shows a distinctive cluster of bands in the 2700–2850 cm⁻¹ region (2719, 2769, 2796, 2845), consistent with an aldehydic C–H Fermi-resonance doublet plus aliphatic C–H stretches (supported by SPC-002 and GFQ-003). Among the candidates, only COCCCCCC=S is a thioaldehyde (R–CH=S), which retains the aldehydic C–H signature while lacking any O–H stretch (absent here, disfavoring the alcohol-containing candidates). The strong C–O stretching expected for an ether around ~1040–1150 cm⁻¹ matches peaks at 1045 and 1130. The 1467 cm⁻¹ band fits aliphatic CH₂/CH₃ bending (GFQ-003). Overall, the presence of aldehydic C–H features and ether C–O stretches best supports candidate 2.
